To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amount of residual heat in laser ablation of metal is determined by the material properties, the laser parameters and the ambient conditions and that it can be reduced by using high laser fluence and high ambient pressure.

1) the residual heat is not homogeneously distributed in the workpiece, but is concentrated in the center of the ablation spot; 2) the residual heat distribution can be described by an exponential decay function; 3) the residual heat depends on the pulse energy and is proportional to the pulse energy; 4) the residual heat increases with increasing pulse repetition rate; 5) the residual heat can be reduced by using a low laser pulse repetition rate and a high pulse energy
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) the determination of the amount of residual heat deposited by an ultra short pulsed Gaussian shaped laser beam in metals, (2) the determination of residual heat in metals after laser irradiation with a high repetition rate and (3) the determination of spatial distribution of the deposited heat in metals.
the following questions: How is the amount of residual heat dependent on the laser parameters and how does it change when the laser pulse shape is changed?
the following aspects: (1) The spatial distribution of the absorbed energy is determined for different pulse durations and repetition rates.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the residual heat is a function of the pulse duration, laser power, repetition rate and the workpiece properties.
, in the case of a Gaussian shaped laser pulse, the amount of residual heat depends on the laser fluence, on the material properties and on the pulse duration.
the residual heat is not uniformly distributed over the whole irradiated area but rather concentrated in a small region at the center of the irradiated area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the residual heat distribution is not only determined by the laser beam shape, but that the material properties and the pulse length also have an influence.
the residual heat is mainly deposited in the center of the irradiated spot.
the residual heat is a function of the laser fluence, the pulse duration, and the repetition rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial distribution of heat is strongly affected by the laser pulse duration.
the spatial distribution of residual heat in ultra short pulsed ablation is strongly influenced by the laser fluence.
the residual heat is not only located at the surface but also in the interior of the workpiece.
